title: Let `.extend()` replace or remove inherited abort signals
summary:
This PR fixes how `.extend()` handles the `signal` option. Before, `deepMergeInternal` always merged the parent signal back in, even when the child used `replaceOption(signal)` or `signal: undefined`. Now a replaced or `undefined` root-level `signal` discards the inherited signals.

The PR also limits signal collection to the root options. A `signal` key inside nested data, such as a `json` body, now merges like any other value. The readme and the `extend` type docs describe the new behavior.

changes.what: `deepMergeInternal` now unwraps `replaceOption` before it handles `signal`. At the root level, a replaced or `undefined` `signal` empties the `signals` list. Only root-level `AbortSignal` values go into `signals`. A comment typo is also fixed.
changes.why: This is the fix. Before, the parent signal stayed in `signals` and overwrote the child value at the end of the merge. `.extend({signal: replaceOption(s)})` now uses only `s`, and `.extend({signal: undefined})` removes the signal.

changes.what: Adds tests for `replaceOption(signal)`, for `signal: undefined`, and for a `signal` key inside `json`. Extends the signal-merging test to abort through the instance signal.
changes.why: The tests cover each branch of the new root-signal logic in `deepMergeInternal`.

changes.what: Adds one paragraph to the `extend` JSDoc: signals are combined, and `replaceOption(signal)` or `signal: undefined` replaces or removes them.
changes.why: Editors show this text, so users find the new behavior where they write the call.

changes.what: Adds the same paragraph to the `.extend()` section.
changes.why: Keeps the readme and the type docs in sync.

flow.caption: `.extend()` merges parent and child options in `deepMergeInternal`. At the root level, it collects each `AbortSignal` in `signals`, and a replaced or `undefined` signal empties the list. `AbortSignal.any` combines what remains.

risks.title: `signal: null` still inherits the parent signal
risks.reason: Line 228 empties `signals` only for `replaceOption` or `undefined`. With `signal: null`, line 285 stores `null`, and lines 312-322 then replace it with the parent signal. `searchParams: null` and `context: null` remove their values, so callers can expect the same here.

tests.description: Call `ky.create({signal: a.signal}).extend({signal: null})`, abort `a`, and check whether the request aborts. Decide if `null` should remove the signal like `undefined`.
Chain `base.extend({signal: replaceOption(b.signal)}).extend({signal: c.signal})`. Abort `b`, then `c`, and confirm each one aborts the request and the base signal does not.
Pass `signal: replaceOption(undefined)` to `.extend()` and confirm the parent signal no longer aborts the request.
Send a POST with `json: {signal: 'x'}` through an extended instance and confirm the server receives `{"signal": "x"}` unchanged.
